units: <cite ref="Megillah 32a:16">Meg. 32ᵃ</cite> he opens (the scroll), sees the place (to read from), <he>גּוֹלֵל ומברך</he> rolls it up again and says the benediction.
<cite ref="Megillah 32a:7">Ib.</cite> <he>הגּוֹלֵל ס״ת וכ׳</he> he who rolls the scrolls up (preparing the place to read from).
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 2:8">B. Mets. II, 8</cite> (<cite ref="Bava Metzia 29b:4">29ᵇ</cite>) <he>גוֹלְלָן</he> he must roll the scrolls over (for the purpose of airing); a. fr.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 21:3">Gen. R. s. 21</cite> (play on <he>גללו</he>, <cite ref="Job 20:7">Job XX, 7</cite>) <he>על שג׳ מצוה וכ׳</he> because he disregarded a light command.
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:14:1">Cant. R. to V, 14</cite> <he>והיו נִגְלָלִין</he> they could be folded up.

Snh. 68ᵃ my two arms which are like two scrolls of the Law שנגללין rolled up (not unfolded, i.e. with me learning is buried which I was prevented from teaching).—Trnsf., with על, to be rolled on top of, to prevail.
<cite ref="Berakhot 7a:3">Ber. 7ᵃ</cite> <he>יִגּוֹלּוּ רחמי על וכ׳</he> may my mercy prevail over my attributes (of justice &c.).
<cite ref="Taanit 21b">Taan. 21ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Menachot 95a:18">Men. 95ᵃ</cite> <he>הוּגְלְלוּ הפרוכות</he> when the curtains (of the Tabernacle) were folded up (for removing).
